# Why OEM Forklift Parts Matter More Than You Think


September 22, 2026


Throughout the northern Midwest, forklifts are relied upon for extensive use.


[Forklift parts](https://materialhandling.altg.com/parts-and-services/parts/) do


need to be replaced from time to time due to natural


wear.


As part of the forklift maintenance process, operators need to find reliable forklift replacement parts to minimize downtime. This often leads to a debate between OEM vs aftermarket forklift parts.


When it comes to deciding between OEM and aftermarket forklift parts, it’s important to understand that OEM forklift parts offer several advantages and


actually matter


more than you might think.


## Why Use OEM Forklift Parts?


To


operate


at peak performance, forklifts need reliable parts. Original equipment


manufacturer


or OEM forklift parts offer the reliability operators need to ensure their equipment is ready to perform. Choosing OEM forklift parts ensures those parts will fit the specific models for which they were manufactured perfectly while also delivering superior performance.


One of the most


important factors


to understand when comparing OEM vs aftermarket forklift parts is that aftermarket parts are not manufactured by the original manufacturer that produced your forklift. Instead, they are produced by external sources. By choosing OEM forklift replacement parts, you can ensure that you are


purchasing


parts from the same manufacturer that produced your forklift.


Since


aftermarket


parts are produced by a third-party manufacturer, they are usually more generic. By comparison, OEM parts are produced to only fit specific forklift models. When you choose to use OEM forklift parts, you never have to be concerned about whether the part will fit your forklift. You can rest assured it will match perfectly.


## Most Common Forklift Replacement Parts


When you


purchase


a brand-new forklift, it always


contains


OEM forklift parts. The question of whether you should use OEM or aftermarket forklift parts comes into play during forklift maintenance and repairs. Due to the nature of how this type of equipment is used, some parts on a forklift tend to wear out sooner than others and need to be replaced more often. These forklift parts include:


**Tires**


Since forklifts are specifically designed to


operate


for


long periods


of time, make precise maneuvers, and transport heavy loads, the tires wear down


frequently


. This results in the need for forklift tire replacements.


**Oil and Air Filters**


Filters


are responsible for


preventing dirt and debris from


impacting


the performance of the engine and ensuring that only clean oil is circulated through the


forklift’s


engine. As a result, filters usually need to be changed


frequently


.


**Pedal Pads**


The rubber pads


located


under the brake and accelerator pedals serve an important purpose by ensuring that the operator’s foot


doesn’t


slip during operation. As they wear down, pedal pads need to be replaced to ensure continued safe operation.


**Forklift Horns**


Forklift horns also serve as an important safety feature and are one of the


most commonly needed


forklift replacement parts.


**Forklift Chains**


Over time, forklift chains will stretch and wear down. When this happens, they must be


immediately


replaced.


**Spark Plugs**


As part of the operation process, exposure to dirt is common.


Unfortunately, that


exposure to dirt can prevent spark plugs from working properly and can


impact


engine performance.


This necessitates the need for routine spark plug replacement for your forklift.


**Batteries**


For forklifts to


operate


at peak efficiency, they must have a properly maintained battery. Signs that a forklift battery needs to be replaced include charges that do not last very


long


or a battery that


seems to be


losing charge.


## The Difference Between OEM vs Aftermarket Forklift Parts


Since OEM parts are designed and built by the same manufacturer that built your forklift, you can be assured that all replacement parts are built to the precise tolerances and specifications


required


. Aftermarket parts are often appealing because they


seem to offer


a less expensive route to obtaining forklift replacement parts. However, aftermarket parts often result in:


- Premature wear


- Reduced performance


- Inconsistent fitting


- Increased equipment failure risk


These risks can become even greater when used in forklifts designed for high-capacity loads.

## Frequently Asked Questions


#### ** Are secondary market parts the same as aftermarket parts?


Yes, secondary market parts are produced by third-party manufacturers and are not genuine OEM forklift parts. They may vary in terms of quality and design.


#### ** Which forklift parts wear out the fastest?


Forklift parts that tend to wear out the fastest include tires, forks, filters, batteries, spark plugs, and water pumps. Regular forklift maintenance and inspections can help to prevent unexpected downtime for replacement.


#### ** How often should forklift parts be replaced?


Required replacement intervals for forklift parts vary based on several factors, including maintenance schedules as recommended by the manufacturer, operating hours, and working conditions


#### ** Can I install forklift parts or must I use a technician?


While it is possible to handle some replacements on your own, such as an air filter, most replacements should be handled by a certified technician. If replacement parts are not installed properly and with the correct tools, it can impact performance and cause serious safety issues.
